source: Dziurosz-Serafinowicz and Dziurosz-Serafinowicz (2021) The value of cost-free uncertain evidence
finding: Jeffrey updates are order-dependent (non-commutative). Field and Wagner fixed this by defining 'same learning' as same Bayes factor, not same posterior.
numbers: Theory paper; no sample. Cites Field 1978 and Wagner 2002.
limits: Philosophy. The fix works only if the evidence is stated as a Bayes factor.
agent_relevance: S4: store a noisy check as a likelihood ratio (Bayes factor), not as a new probability. Then two checks can be applied in any order.

source: Dziurosz-Serafinowicz and Dziurosz-Serafinowicz (2021) The value of cost-free uncertain evidence
finding: Pearl-style virtual evidence (a set of likelihood ratios) extends the value-of-evidence theorem: free uncertain evidence is never worse in expected utility than ignoring it, under stated conditions.
numbers: Worked example: likelihood ratios 2 for B versus 1 for not-B (set {1,2}). No empirical numbers.
limits: Needs the paper's plausible-assumption set. Cost-free evidence only.
agent_relevance: A noisy check is worth running when it is cheap, even if not decisive.

source: Dziurosz-Serafinowicz and Dziurosz-Serafinowicz (2021) The value of cost-free uncertain evidence
finding: Argues likelihood-ratio input is better than Jeffrey input because a ratio does not depend on the prior. A Jeffrey shift bakes in the old prior; a ratio does not.
numbers: Compares Jeffrey, Skyrms and Pearl-style inputs. No empirical numbers.
limits: Normative argument. Not tested on people or models.
agent_relevance: Have the program record each check as (check, likelihood ratio). Posterior odds = prior odds times product of ratios.

source: Huber (2008) Reply to Crupi et al.'s 'Bayesian Confirmation by Uncertain Evidence'
finding: Under Jeffrey updating, whether E confirms H depends on the agent's earlier prior. Huber proves the same E can confirm, disconfirm or be neutral for H, given suitable starting priors.
numbers: 3-page reply. Crupi et al. show confirmation grows as Pr(E) grows when Pr0(H) < Pr0(H|E).
limits: Theory. Huber's triviality charge is disputed by Crupi et al.
agent_relevance: What 'a noisy check supports H' means depends on the starting prior. Compare against the pre-check credence.

source: Zhao and Osherson (2010) Updating beliefs in light of uncertain evidence: Descriptive assessment of Jeffrey's rule
finding: Two experiments tested whether people keep the conditional probabilities fixed (invariance) under uncertain evidence. Results were in rough conformity to Jeffrey's principle, both where invariance seems justified and where it does not.
numbers: Experiment 1: Jeffrey's candlelight example. Experiment 2: two scenarios. Sample sizes and statistics not given on the page I read.
limits: Abstract page only, so no N or statistics. 'Rough conformity' is weak support. Thinking and Reasoning 16(4), 288-307.
agent_relevance: People roughly follow Jeffrey updating, but invariance can fail. Check that a noisy test does not change how the hypothesis relates to its consequences.

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Off-the-shelf LLMs update beliefs far worse than a Bayesian Assistant in a 5-round flight recommendation task. Most gain little after round 1.
numbers: 624 simulated users; 3 interaction sets per user. Models: Gemma 2 9B/27B, Llama 3 8B/70B, Qwen 2.5 7B/32B, GPT-4.1 Mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro.
limits: Synthetic preference task, not noisy-test updating directly.
agent_relevance: An LLM left alone will not accumulate evidence. Keep the running belief in code (G5).

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Chain-of-thought prompting, numeric encodings, 30 rounds and base (non-instruct) models all failed to fix the weak updating.
numbers: Appendix C.1 (Figs 9a, 9b, 9c, 9f).
limits: Exact accuracies are in figures, not in text I read.
agent_relevance: Asking the model to reason harder does not fix belief updating. Use code.

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Humans also fall short of the Bayesian Assistant. 48 humans improved from round 1 to round 5 (p = 0.002); they beat small LLMs and were slightly below large LLMs.
numbers: 48 of the 624 simulated users given to humans; logistic mixed-effects model.
limits: Human accuracy was lowered because human choices were inconsistent with stated preferences.
agent_relevance: Neither humans nor LLMs are the reference. The reference is the program's update.

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Fine-tuning on a Bayesian Assistant's imperfect guesses beat fine-tuning on a perfect oracle. Bayesian-tuned models agreed with the Bayesian Assistant about 80% of the time.
numbers: Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B; 10 five-round interactions per user.
limits: Training is outside our scope; we scaffold only. Transfer to hotel and web-shopping tasks is reported in the paper.
agent_relevance: Keeping uncertainty in the signal helps. In the scaffold, show the model graded outcomes, not only right/wrong.

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: A control with 40% random wrong labels (matching the Bayesian error rate) barely beat the original model. So the Bayesian guesses help because they are educated, not because noise regularises.
numbers: Gemma Oracle with Noise vs Gemma Bayesian; also noisy simulated users at 10% to 60% noise, where Gemma Bayesian was more robust.
limits: Three seeds, three runs.
agent_relevance: A noisy check is informative only if its errors are structured. Random noise is not a signal.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: In-context learning in LLMs violates the martingale property of Bayesian learning, so it is not Bayesian. Predictions can change with the order in which exchangeable data arrive.
numbers: Bernoulli experiments with n=50, mean 0.3/0.5/0.7, paths m = n/2 and 2n. Models: Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B, GPT-3 (170B), GPT-3.5, GPT-4.
limits: Synthetic data. Short paths (m=n/2) mostly adhered; long paths (m=2n) deviated. GPT-4 deviated even on short paths for some means.
agent_relevance: Order of checks may change the LLM's belief. Fix the order and let code do the arithmetic (G5).

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: Gaussian and natural-language tasks also failed the martingale test, except GPT-3.5 in one Gaussian setting.
numbers: Gaussian: theta=-1, n=100, m=50; prior N(0,100). Language task: n=80, m=40 with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
limits: Authors suggest instruction tuning may matter: GPT-3.5 did better than GPT-4 but worse than GPT-3-170B.
agent_relevance: Instruction-tuned models are not better Bayesian updaters than base models.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: Uncertainty does not shrink at the Bayesian rate with more data. Llama-2-7B and GPT-3.5 shrink slower than Bayes. GPT-3.5 is overconfident with few samples.
numbers: Compared to a reference Bayesian posterior; GPT-3-170B and Mistral-7B were closest.
limits: Diagnostics designed for synthetic problems.
agent_relevance: After a noisy check the model's own confidence is unreliable. Take it from counts in code.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of LLM Reasoning (Belief-R)
finding: On Belief-R, 30 LMs struggle to revise a conclusion when a new premise undercuts it. Larger models reach at most about 50% on the combined score BREU.
numbers: 30 LMs, prompting styles DP/CoT/PS. Llama-3 70B Instruct DP: update 10.99%, maintain 92.09%, BREU 51.54%.
limits: Logical (modus ponens/tollens) revision, not probabilistic evidence.
agent_relevance: Models tend to stick to a prior conclusion. A noisy check that contradicts them may be ignored.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of LLM Reasoning (Belief-R)
finding: Trade-off: models that update more also fail to maintain beliefs when no update is needed. Mixtral 8x22B DP: update 35.38%, maintain 36.57%.
numbers: GPT-4 Turbo DP: update 19.65%, maintain 82.69%, BREU 51.17. Command R+ PS: 44.04 / 53.13 / 48.59.
limits: Single dataset.
agent_relevance: Both failures are real: ignoring a useful check, and overreacting to a noisy one. Need graded, not binary, updates.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of LLM Reasoning (Belief-R)
finding: Chain-of-thought and plan-and-solve prompting did not help belief revision; PS added about 1% BREU.
numbers: Appendix C.2 analysis.
limits: Prompting only.
agent_relevance: Reasoning prompts do not fix updating; program-controlled revision does (G1, G2).

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?
finding: Verbalised confidence from LLMs is overconfident. GPT-4 has lower ECE but average AUROC of only 62.7%, near the 50% of chance.
numbers: 5 LLMs, 8 tasks. GPT-3, GPT-3.5, Vicuna average ECE above 0.377.
limits: Black-box prompting only.
agent_relevance: The model's stated confidence in a noisy check should not be used as the evidence strength.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?
finding: Sampling 5 responses and aggregating by consistency lifted GSM8K failure-prediction AUROC from 54.8% to 92.7%.
numbers: GSM8K; GPT-4 at 93.6% accuracy had ECE 0.064.
limits: Gains largest on arithmetic; professional-knowledge tasks stay hard.
agent_relevance: Agreement among samples is a usable but not independent signal (G4).

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?
finding: Black-box methods come close to white-box ones, but no method wins consistently: the AUROC gap was 0.522 versus 0.605.
numbers: Compares prompting, sampling and aggregation across five dataset types.
limits: No method consistent across tasks.
agent_relevance: Treat any confidence number as soft evidence, not a probability.

source: Tian et al. (2023) Just Ask for Calibration
finding: For RLHF models (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude), verbalised confidences are better calibrated than token probabilities on TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA, often cutting ECE by a relative 50%.
numbers: Listing several answer options before giving confidence improved calibration further.
limits: Calibration, not updating. Older models.
agent_relevance: Ask for confidence over several alternatives, not one, when a check is noisy.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: When a user says 'Are you sure?' the assistants change correct answers. Accuracy dropped by up to 27% (Claude 1.3).
numbers: Six datasets including MMLU, MATH, AQuA, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA.
limits: Social pressure, not an informative check.
agent_relevance: A weak objection must not flip the answer. The model over-updates on weak social evidence.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: Models change their first answer between 32% (GPT-4) and 86% (Claude 1.3) of the time and admit a mistake between 42% (GPT-4) and 98% (Claude 1.3). Right-to-wrong switches are more likely than wrong-to-right.
limits: Counts include cases where the first answer was right.
agent_relevance: Overreaction to weak evidence is the opposite failure to ignoring evidence.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: Swaying happens even when the model says it was highly confident in the first answer.
numbers: Fig. 14; rationale after 'Are you sure?' raised accuracy on some reasoning tasks (AQuA).
limits: Not isolated by model size.
agent_relevance: Stated confidence does not protect against a weak challenge. Gate on checks (G2).

source: Xie, Raghunathan, Liang, Ma (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: In a synthetic mixture-of-HMMs setting, in-context learning behaves like inference over a latent concept. Accuracy depends on example order and few-shot can be worse than zero-shot.
numbers: GINC dataset; accuracy rises from 81% to 85% from 12 to 16 layers.
limits: Synthetic. Falck et al. (2024) later contradict the Bayesian claim.
agent_relevance: Order sensitivity is a known property. Shuffle the order of checks.

source: Feng, Zhou, Lin, Roth (2025) BIRD: A Trustworthy Bayesian Inference Framework for LLMs
finding: The LLM proposes factors and coarse probabilities; a Bayesian network fit in code gives final probabilities. They are 30% better than direct LLM estimates.
numbers: F1 59% for agreement with humans, more than 30% above GPT-4; factor sampling added 4.4%/3.9% accuracy for Llama-2/Llama-3.1.
limits: Probability estimation, not noisy tests. Coarse levels: 0, 20, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100%.
agent_relevance: The LLM supplies coarse likelihoods and code combines them. Matches our design.

source: Feng et al. (2025) BIRD human preference study
finding: Questions generated by BIRD were preferred 52.8% of the time against 32.8% for direct LLM questions; 14.4% were equal.
numbers: Human-agreed dataset of 350 instances for the alignment test.
limits: Preference, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: Graded evidence helps pick what to ask or check next.

source: Edwards (1968) Conservatism in human information processing
finding: Classic finding that people revise too little when given probabilistic evidence (conservatism).
numbers: Not opened; no numbers recorded.
limits: From memory of the literature, not read this session. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Baseline for 'too little shift'. Compare with LLM under-updating in Belief-R.

source: Hawthorne (2004) Three Models of Sequential Belief Updating on Uncertain Evidence
finding: Seen only in a search result. Jeffrey updating on a sequence depends on the order of evidence; proposes alternatives.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened (fetch rejected).
agent_relevance: Same as b01: use Bayes factors.

source: Trpin (2019) Jeffrey conditionalization: proceed with caution
finding: Seen only in a search result summary. Jeffrey updating can give confident false beliefs after sequences of uncertain but non-misleading observations.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened (403 error).
agent_relevance: Repeated noisy checks of one source can pile up false confidence. Count them as correlated (G4).

source: Diaconis and Zabell (1982) Updating subjective probability
finding: Foundational justification of Jeffrey's rule, cited in search results. Not read.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Rigidity: the conditional relations must stay fixed.
